title: Headless mode (--headless) stalls after ~25-55s when any scene is loaded as main scene, even a completely empty one
body:
### Godot version

4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GPU - AMD Ryzen (16 threads)

Also reproduced on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 via WSL2), same Godot 4.7.1-stable official Linux build, so this does not appear to be OS-specific.

### Issue description

Running Godot headless (`--headless`) with **any** scene as the main scene — including a completely empty scene containing a single `Control` node with no script and no resources — causes the process to almost completely stall after roughly 25 to 55 seconds of real (wall-clock) time. It is not a hard freeze/deadlock: the process keeps consuming roughly 20-30% of one CPU core, but makes almost no forward progress (frame-to-frame game time barely advances relative to real time elapsed).

A `--script some_scene_tree.gd` invocation that overrides `MainLoop`/`SceneTree` directly and never loads or instantiates any scene (`current_scene` stays unset, no `.tscn` is ever loaded) does **not** exhibit this issue — it runs indefinitely at full speed with no slowdown.

This makes any sufficiently long headless run (batch testing, CI, automated balance/perf testing, `--quit-after` with a very high frame count, etc.) effectively unusable past the ~25-55s mark, even though the exact same scene runs completely normally when launched normally (windowed).

Investigated in depth before reporting:
- Not caused by antivirus, third-party firewall, a paired Bluetooth controller, the GPU rendering driver (reproduces identically with `--rendering-driver dummy`), or the render loop itself (reproduces identically with `--disable-render-loop`).
- Confirmed via Process Monitor (Windows) that during the stall there is essentially zero file/registry/network activity — ruling out any external I/O cause.
- Confirmed via WinDbg (`cdb -p <pid> -c "~*kb"`) that during the stall the **main thread is actively executing** (not blocked/waiting) deep inside the engine's own code (many nested call frames, unfortunately no public symbols available for the official release build to identify the exact function). All `WorkerThreadPool` threads (one per CPU core) are simultaneously idle and correctly waiting on `SleepConditionVariableSRW`, so this is not worker-pool starvation or a classic two-thread deadlock.
- Ruled out our own project's autoloads/gameplay code as the root cause: the same stall reproduces on a project reduced to a single empty `Control` scene with **no autoloads, no scripts, no resources at all**.
- Ruled out `--quit-after`'s frame-count handling specifically (reproduces with or without that flag).
- Ruled out Jolt Physics (reproduces with the default 3D physics engine too, even though the project is 2D-only).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a brand-new empty Godot 4.7.1 project (any renderer).
2. Add a single scene `empty.tscn` containing only one `Control` node, no script.
3. Set it as the project's main scene (or pass it explicitly on the command line).
4. Run: `godot --headless --path . res://empty.tscn --quit-after 999999`
5. Observe: the process starts normally, then somewhere between ~25 and ~55 seconds of real time, forward progress essentially stops (CPU usage stays non-zero, around 20-30% of one core, but the process makes almost no further progress and never reaches the frame count needed to quit).

For comparison, step 6 below does **not** reproduce the issue:
6. Run the same project via a custom `--script` that extends `SceneTree`, overrides `_process()`, and never touches `current_scene`/never loads any `.tscn`. This runs indefinitely at full speed.

### Minimal reproduction project

Will attach a minimal project (a single empty `Control` scene) if useful — happy to prepare one on request. The repro is small enough that it may be simpler to reproduce directly from the steps above.
